cards.back: eunuch (palace servant castrated to serve the emperor)
cards.example: 朱棣派太监郑和出使西洋。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zhu Di sent the eunuch Zheng He on diplomatic missions to the Western Seas.
cards.breakdown: 太：超过（大）一点点，表示最高、最大的 · 监：像眼睛从上往下看（臣），确保一切在掌控中

cards.back: move the capital (to a new city)
cards.example: 明成祖把首都从南京迁到了北京。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Yongle Emperor moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing.
cards.breakdown: 迁：在道路上（辶）走向另一处（西），搬迁移动 · 都：聚集了所有人（者）的大城市（邑）

cards.back: to harbor great ambitions / have big dreams in one's heart
cards.example: 朱棣是一位胸怀大志的皇帝。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zhu Di was an emperor who harbored great ambitions.
cards.breakdown: 胸：身体（月）里有一个藏东西的腔 · 怀：心里（忄）藏着某人或某事 · 志：心（心）里记住的目标，是人的志向

cards.back: to rule / govern ★复习L8
cards.example: 在朱棣的统治下，明朝越来越强大。
cards.exampleTranslation: Under Zhu Di's rule, the Ming Dynasty grew stronger and stronger.
cards.breakdown: 统：丝线（纟）把所有东西统统串在一起 · 治：用水（氵）把台地上的洪水治理好

cards.back: to surrender and submit (to a new ruler)
cards.example: 郑克塽归顺清朝，台湾归入清政府管辖。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng Keshuang submitted to the Qing, and Taiwan came under Qing rule.
cards.breakdown: 归：从远处回来，回到原来的地方 · 顺：沿着河流（川）的方向顺势而为，不再抵抗

cards.back: to go on a diplomatic mission (represent one's country abroad)
cards.example: 郑和出使西洋，访问了许多国家。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng He went on diplomatic missions to the Western Seas, visiting many countries.
cards.breakdown: 出：从山洞里走出来，超越了原来的界限 · 使：人（亻）奉命出发，代表国家去办事

cards.back: prestige / high reputation that commands respect
cards.example: 郑和的出使提高了明朝的威望。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng He's voyages raised the Ming Dynasty's prestige.
cards.breakdown: 威：手持武器的士兵（戌）让人感到敬畏 · 望：站在高处眺望，月亮让人仰望

cards.back: to promote / advance / help something grow
cards.example: 郑和的出使促进了中外文化交流。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng He's voyages promoted cultural exchange between China and the world.
cards.breakdown: 促：人（亻）的脚步（足）加快，催促前进 · 进：向前走（辶），越走越好

cards.back: cultural exchange (sharing ideas, art, and learning between countries)
cards.example: 郑和的出使促进了中外文化交流。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng He's voyages promoted cultural exchange between China and the world.
cards.breakdown: 交：人叉开双腿，两边互相交换 · 流：水（氵）不停地流动，传播开去

cards.back: to migrate / immigrant (person who moves to another land)
cards.example: 广东、福建移民南洋的人渐渐多了起来。
cards.exampleTranslation: The number of migrants from Guangdong and Fujian to Southeast Asia gradually increased.
cards.breakdown: 移：将庄稼（禾）搬到别处，表示移动 · 民：古代表示被统治的人民

cards.back: missionary (person sent to spread their religion in a foreign land)
cards.example: 意大利传教士利玛窦来中国传教。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Italian missionary Matteo Ricci came to China to spread his religion.
cards.breakdown: 传：人（亻）手把手（专）传递，一代传一代 · 教：大人拿棍子（攵）教孩子（子）在屋里学习 · 士：有知识有担当的人，站得笔直

cards.back: layout / arrangement (how a city or space is planned out)
cards.example: 北京的城市建筑布局严整，街道笔直。
cards.exampleTranslation: Beijing's city layout was well-organized, with perfectly straight streets.
cards.breakdown: 布：用手把织好的布料摊开，铺展开来 · 局：口（空间）中有一把尺，规划整齐的格局

cards.back: perfectly straight (like a ruler, not curved at all)
cards.example: 北京的街道笔直，一眼望到头。
cards.exampleTranslation: Beijing's streets are perfectly straight, visible all the way to the end.
cards.breakdown: 笔：竹（竹）制的毛笔，笔管直直的 · 直：十个眼睛一起看，看得非常直

cards.back: resplendent and magnificent (gleaming gold and jade — used for grand palaces)
cards.example: 故宫金碧辉煌，是世界上最大的古代宫殿。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Forbidden City is resplendent and magnificent — the world's largest ancient palace.
cards.breakdown: 金：地下埋着的闪光金属 · 碧：石头中绿色的宝玉 · 辉：光芒四射照耀一切 · 煌：火光如王者般明亮耀眼

cards.back: masterpiece (an outstanding, extraordinary work)
cards.example: 北京古城是古代城市建筑的杰作。
cards.exampleTranslation: Ancient Beijing is a masterpiece of ancient city architecture.
cards.breakdown: 杰：树木（木）上有鸟（大），站得比别人高 · 作：人（亻）突然（乍）动起来，开始做事

cards.back: vast / massive in scale (used for huge projects or endeavors)
cards.example: 明朝修复长城，工程浩大。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Ming Dynasty restored the Great Wall — a massive engineering project.
cards.breakdown: 浩：水（氵）势滔天，浩浩荡荡，极其广大 · 大：一个人叉开双手双脚，表示非常大

cards.back: to restore / repair (bring something damaged back to its original state)
cards.example: 明朝修复了长城，使它更加坚固。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Ming Dynasty restored the Great Wall, making it stronger.
cards.breakdown: 修：用手（攵）整理仪容（彡），精心修缮 · 复：走回来，回到原来的地方

cards.back: handicraft industry (goods made by hand, like pottery, silk weaving)
cards.example: 农村多余的劳动力流入了手工业与商业。
cards.exampleTranslation: Surplus rural labor flowed into the handicraft industry and commerce.
cards.breakdown: 手：张开的手掌，五指分明 · 工：像一把尺子，表示工作和技艺 · 业：像书架一排排竖立，表示一项事业

cards.back: exquisite / skillfully crafted (delicate and cleverly made)
cards.example: 明朝手工业技术精巧，产品远销海外。
cards.exampleTranslation: Ming handicraft techniques were exquisite, with products sold far overseas.
cards.breakdown: 精：用精选的米（米）加上青色，精益求精 · 巧：工（工）匠的手艺刚刚好，不差毫厘

cards.back: scale / scope (how big an operation or project is)
cards.example: 明朝手工业生产规模不断扩大。
cards.exampleTranslation: The scale of handicraft production in the Ming Dynasty kept expanding.
cards.breakdown: 规：用圆规画圆，定出规矩 · 模：木头（木）刻出的标准样板，用来模仿

cards.back: employment / to hire workers (paying someone to work for you)
cards.example: 明朝出现了雇佣关系，窑主雇工成百上千。
cards.exampleTranslation: Employer-employee relationships emerged in the Ming, with kiln owners hiring hundreds of workers.
cards.breakdown: 雇：像雇鸟（隹）一样用钱财换来劳力 · 佣：人（亻）受雇于人，是有偿的用工（用）

cards.back: employer (the person or company that hires and pays workers)
cards.example: 富人为雇主，雇有长工和短工。
cards.exampleTranslation: Wealthy people were employers who hired long-term and short-term workers.
cards.breakdown: 雇：用钱财换来劳力 · 主：一盏灯的主心骨，是主人的标志

cards.back: international (involving or between different countries)
cards.example: 明朝在国际贸易中是顺差。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Ming Dynasty ran a surplus in international trade.
cards.breakdown: 国：口（边界）里有一块宝玉（玉），守护着领土 · 际：两堆土（阝）靠在一起，交界的地方

cards.back: trade surplus (exporting more than you import — money flows in)
cards.example: 明朝出口多于进口，在国际贸易中是顺差。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Ming exported more than it imported, running a surplus in international trade.
cards.breakdown: 顺：沿着流水方向，顺势而为，正向的 · 差：表示差额，这里指贸易的差额

cards.back: silver (used as money — China imported huge amounts through trade)
cards.example: 明朝出口瓷器和丝绸，换取了大量的白银。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Ming exported porcelain and silk in exchange for large amounts of silver.
cards.breakdown: 白：太阳刚升起，光芒洁白 · 银：金属（钅）中坚硬（艮）闪亮的那种，是货币

cards.back: to lead / be at the forefront (ahead of everyone else)
cards.example: 明朝时中国传统科技处于世界领先的地位。
cards.exampleTranslation: During the Ming, China's traditional science and technology held a world-leading position.
cards.breakdown: 领：发号施令（令）的那个头（页）· 先：人先走一步，走在别人前面

cards.back: monumental work / great book (a major, important literary or scientific work)
cards.example: 明朝科学家写出了三部科学巨著。
cards.exampleTranslation: Ming scientists wrote three monumental works of science.
cards.breakdown: 巨：握着大工具的手，极大的意思 · 著：像草（艹）一样扎根（者），写出有分量的作品

cards.back: vigorous / flourishing (growing energetically, full of life)
cards.example: 明代是中国古典小说蓬勃发展的时期。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Ming era was a period of vigorous development for classical Chinese novels.
cards.breakdown: 蓬：草（艹）长得蓬蓬乱乱（逢），生机勃勃 · 勃：用力气（力）像脉搏一样充满活力

cards.back: the Renaissance (European cultural rebirth in art and science, 14th–17th c.)
cards.example: 明朝和欧洲的文艺复兴处于同一时期。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Ming Dynasty was in the same era as Europe's Renaissance.
cards.breakdown: 文：花纹图案，后来表示文字文化 · 艺：从小慢慢长出来的本领 · 复：走回来，回到原来的地方 · 兴：大家把东西高高托起来，欣欣向荣

cards.back: to fall behind / lag behind (become less advanced than others)
cards.example: 从文艺复兴以后，中国开始渐渐落后了。
cards.exampleTranslation: After the Renaissance, China gradually began to fall behind.
cards.breakdown: 落：草木往下掉，像雨水落下 · 后：在后面迟迟不来，表示落在后面

cards.back: to break out / erupt suddenly (war, rebellion, volcano)
cards.example: 明朝后期爆发了李自成领导的农民起义。
cards.exampleTranslation: In the late Ming, a peasant uprising led by Li Zicheng broke out.
cards.breakdown: 爆：火（火）和暴（暴）结合，忽然猛烈地发生 · 发：手拉弓，把东西射发出去

cards.back: peasant uprising (farmers rise up and rebel against their rulers)
cards.example: 1644年，农民起义军攻入北京，明朝灭亡。
cards.exampleTranslation: In 1644, peasant rebel troops captured Beijing and the Ming Dynasty fell.
cards.breakdown: 农：在田野里弯腰劳作的人 · 起：自己（己）走起来，出发行动 · 义：心里有善良，愿意牺牲自己

cards.back: to resist the Qing (fighting against Qing rule after Ming fell)
cards.example: 郑成功是著名的抗清名将。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng Chenggong was a famous general who resisted the Qing.
cards.breakdown: 抗：用手（扌）高举（亢），不肯低头 · 清：水（氵）清澈，是清朝的国号

cards.back: to recover / recapture (take back lost land) ★复习L7
cards.example: 郑成功打败荷兰人，收复了台湾。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng Chenggong defeated the Dutch and recovered Taiwan.
cards.breakdown: 收：用手（攵）把散落的东西收拢起来 · 复：走回来，回到原来的地方

cards.back: to establish / start up (schools, businesses, organizations)
cards.example: 郑成功在台湾兴办工商业，开办学堂。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng Chenggong established industry, commerce, and schools in Taiwan.
cards.breakdown: 兴：大家一起把东西高高托起来，欣欣向荣 · 办：两边用力施压（力），把事情办成

cards.back: Ming Dynasty (1368–1644) – founded by Zhu Yuanzhang, capital at Nanjing then Beijing
cards.example: 明朝是一个经济繁荣、对外关系比较开放的朝代。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Ming Dynasty was a dynasty with a prosperous economy and relatively open foreign relations.

cards.back: Zhu Yuanzhang – founder of Ming Dynasty, first emperor ★复习L8
cards.example: 公元1368年朱元璋建立明朝，定都南京。
cards.exampleTranslation: In 1368 CE, Zhu Yuanzhang founded the Ming Dynasty and set the capital at Nanjing.

cards.back: Yongle Emperor Zhu Di – 3rd Ming emperor, moved capital to Beijing, sent Zheng He's voyages
cards.example: 明成祖朱棣胸怀大志，把首都从南京迁到了北京。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Yongle Emperor Zhu Di harbored great ambitions and moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing.

cards.back: Zheng He – Ming eunuch admiral who led seven great voyages to Southeast Asia, India, and Africa
cards.example: 郑和带领船队出使西洋，提高了明朝的威望。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng He led a fleet on diplomatic missions to the Western Seas, raising Ming's prestige.

cards.back: Li Zicheng – peasant rebel leader who captured Beijing in 1644, ending the Ming Dynasty
cards.example: 李自成领导农民起义，1644年攻入北京，明朝灭亡。
cards.exampleTranslation: Li Zicheng led a peasant uprising and captured Beijing in 1644, ending the Ming Dynasty.

cards.back: Zheng Chenggong (Koxinga) – anti-Qing general who recovered Taiwan from the Dutch
cards.example: 郑成功打败荷兰人，收复台湾，是民族英雄。
cards.exampleTranslation: Zheng Chenggong defeated the Dutch, recovered Taiwan, and is a national hero.

cards.back: Xu Guangqi – Ming scientist who co-translated Euclid's Elements with Matteo Ricci
cards.example: 徐光启和利玛窦一起翻译了《几何原本》。
cards.exampleTranslation: Xu Guangqi and Matteo Ricci co-translated Euclid's Elements.

cards.back: Matteo Ricci (1552–1610) – Italian Jesuit missionary who brought Western science to China
cards.example: 意大利传教士利玛窦把西方科学知识传到中国。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Italian missionary Matteo Ricci brought Western scientific knowledge to China.
